summary: Pocahontas County site registered 2017; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it unconfirmed, and a topo listing calls it historical. No build or removal dates found.

facts.status_note: Listed as unconfirmed; no source we read confirms a tower here.

events.note: Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register January 26, 2017; nominated by Brian M. Powell

evidence.supports: Site is in Pocahontas County, West Virginia
Register page is the only description of the site; it says nothing about remains or access
Topo listing gives the USGS map as Edray, WV
evidence.quote: It can be seen on the USGS 1:24K topographic map Edray, WV

evidence.supports: Topo listing names a Gay Knob Fire Tower (historical) in Pocahontas County
evidence.quote: Gay Knob Fire Tower (historical) is a locale located in Pocahontas County, WV
at an elevation of 4524 ft MSL

evidence.supports: Association list marks the site unconfirmed with type unknown
evidence.quote: Gay Knob Pocahontas 38.31722 -80.07028 Unconfirmed Unknown FFLOS US 1683, WV 74

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks Gay Knob Unconfirmed with type Unknown. No source we read confirms a tower stood here or that it was removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 4,522 ft (1,378 m); the TopoQuest listing gives 4524 ft. The story uses the register figure. The gap is small and may be rounding or a different survey point.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. The register page has coordinates, elevation, registration date and a nominator, but no description, build date, staffing or removal date. A USGS-based topo listing calls it the Gay Knob Fire Tower (historical), which suggests an old tower name but is not proof a tower stood. The Association list marks it Unconfirmed, so the brief's gone status is not supported. Gay Knob is not in the Monongahela National Forest USDA fire tower history, and the Forest Lookouts West Virginia page has no entry for it. The story is short (about 90 words) because nothing more is supported. A future pass could check historical USGS Edray maps or Forest Service records.
